headline: Protein language model embeddings guide enzyme discovery and structural proximity tests
label: Protein Representation Guided Engineering
summary: Protein language model embeddings and structure predictors are now used to navigate enzyme sequence space and test catalytic site proximity.
synthesis: The dominant thread is using protein sequence and structure representations to prioritize or interpret biological choices. SelectZyme embeds enzyme sequences with an alignment-free protein language model, reduces dimensionality, and applies HDBSCAN clustering to support interactive visualization and mining of more than 100,000 sequences. The metabolic study benchmarks AlphaFold2/3, ESMFold and HDOCK on low-affinity dimers and scores consecutive enzyme pairs in E. coli, finding no evidence of spatial optimization of catalytic site proximity. HORI-EN pairs atomic-level energetic scoring with higher-order residue clique analysis to predict mutational hotspots in protein structures. GIDEON, an ILP framework for yeast genetic interaction networks, addresses compensatory pathways and is less directly tied to protein representations. What is new here is navigation of enzyme sequence space for discovery and mining, alongside tests of predicted structures against biological proximity.
